title: ARPAPED Capability Manifest
description: Machine-readable declaration of a capability contract and the executor references that implement it. Lives with the capability's generic footprint (R3), one entry per implementation. Consumed by the generic assembler during the Publish phase (Phase 8) to build and register implementation records into the canonical Registry.

capability_id.description: Generic capability identity per R1 as domain.operation. Never product-prefixed.

contract.description: Path or identity of the contract artifact that machine-defines this capability (R2).

contract_version.description: Version of the capability contract this manifest binds to.

implementation_id.description: Unique identifier of this implementation record.

executor.description: Reference to the executor. For executor_kind 'direct' or 'factory' (the default 'direct'), this is 'module:attr'. For executor_kind 'process', this instead names a program to run, spawned once at assembly time and reached over an out-of-process protocol that mirrors the same execute(operation, input, policy) -> output contract. The component is reached only by the Bridge; it never registers itself. When executor_kind is 'factory', 'module:attr' names a factory — (dependencies) -> executor — called once at assembly time.

executor_kind.description: 'direct' (default): executor IS the registration-unaware executor. 'factory': executor is invoked once at assembly time with a Dependencies scoped to this contract's dependencies.capabilities (R4), and its return value becomes the executor — for a capability that needs live access to another capability during its own execution, not just pre-computed input from its caller. 'process': executor names a program, spawned once at assembly time, that becomes the executor — for a capability implemented in a language other than the resolved Bridge's own (bridge/MANIFEST.yaml).

priority.description: Higher number = higher precedence = selected first among candidates that already match a request's other constraints (version, policy, health). No default: every implementation must state its own precedence explicitly rather than silently inheriting an implicit one (2-RULES.md 'The Registry contract').
